title: Selling friction instead of convenience
prompt: fill the gaps on this, it's half baked. what if a company sold the opposite of convenience. like every app makes things easier and somehow we're all emptier. what if you paid for friction on purpose, things that are deliberately hard, slow, done by hand, and the hardness IS the product. not a hobby shop, more like... a business model built on the fact that meaning comes from effort. maybe it's a subscription, maybe it's a place, i don't know. i keep thinking people don't actually want to save time, they want to spend it on something that feels like theirs

title: A company built to finish
prompt: i can't put this into words yet. a startup that's designed from day one to shut itself down. not fail, finish. like it has a mission and when the mission is done the company dissolves and gives everything away. every company is built to live forever and maybe that's the problem, they outlive their reason and turn into something else. i guess it's like a mortal company? not sure if that's genius or just naive. say what i mean

title: A bank for time, not money
prompt: help me articulate this. a bank but for time, not money. you deposit hours now, when you have energy, and someone gives them back to you later when you need them, like when you're old or sick or have a newborn. the strangers in between do the actual work. it's not volunteering and it's not a gig app, it's more like a promise between generations? maybe it needs money in it somewhere, maybe that ruins it. something about trust being the currency

title: An anti-advertising company
prompt: fill the gaps, i can't say this right yet. what if there was a company that sold you nothing, it just paid you to stop wanting things. like an anti-advertising company. every ad is someone being paid to make you want more, so what if someone got paid to make you want less, and that was the business. maybe you subscribe to it, maybe brands pay to be left alone by it, i don't know. it's not minimalism exactly, minimalism became its own shopping category. i guess it's more about getting your attention back? and honestly maybe i just want this because i'm tired of wanting things all the time

title: Teachers you could watch not know
prompt: fill the gaps on this. i keep thinking the best teachers i had weren't the ones who explained things well, they were the ones who were obviously still confused about something themselves, like you could watch them not know. and i guess it made it ok to not know. i want to build something around that but every learning product is built on the expert who has it all figured out. maybe it's a course where the teacher is only one step ahead? maybe that's just a worse course. not sure
